items.quote: for e = 1, B64[byte(s, 9 + (id % 4096) * 7)] do
items.what: The graph node-record layout (header n(2), then 7-char records cell(3) layer(1) component(2) degree(1)) is restated as independent magic offsets in three places: decodeGraph (PathGrid.lua:500-508, pos = 3, pos + 6, pos + 7), metadata (528-529, 3 + (id % 4096) * 7, pos + 3, pos + 4) and adjacent (541, the precomputed 9 + i * 7 for the degree byte). Canonical home: metadata's record position (one RECORD = 7 / header offset), with adjacent reusing it (pos + 6).
items.why: The encoder is the spec: tools/baker/gen_nav.py:677-679 writes enc(len, 2) then enc(cell,3)+enc(layer,1)+enc(comp,2)+enc(degree,1), documented in the generated header (gen_nav.py:738-739). Cross-language restatement in the decoder is unavoidable; the intra-file restatement is not: '9' folds header + degree offset into one literal that no longer reads as either, so a record-width or header change to the encoder must be found in three decoder sites. Not a hot-loop inline: adjacent decodes once per entrance and caches (549).

local function OnUpdate(pin, elapsed)
	if not (GameTooltip:IsOwned(pin) and GameTooltip:IsShown()) then
		pin:SetScript("OnUpdate", nil)
		return
	end
	pin.elapsed = pin.elapsed + elapsed

		pin.elapsed = pin.elapsed % 1
		Tooltip(pin)
	end
end

items.quote: I wanted a proper "get me there" for WoW: Forever, so Shortest Path Forever finds the fastest way across the world. Shift-click a destination on the map, or pick a quest, and it joins walking paths, flight paths, boats, zeppelins, lifts, the Deeprun Tram, portals and your hearthstone or class teleports into one journey. Directions use the game's own waypoint marker, map pins and objective tracker, so it looks like it came with the game. Walking maps for Eastern Kingdoms, Kalimdor and Zephras Isle come in the same download.

Differences: map_canvas's point() returns None for an unprojectable point while render_stops' point() assumes projection succeeds (fine for the fixed Loch Modan scene, but a missing assignment would surface as a TypeError rather than a skip); the rest is identical. items.reason: The small-idiom exclusion applies: both renderers already share map_base, projection, flush_strokes and map_landmarks; the repeated code assembles their canvases. Their contracts differ: map_canvas tolerates unprojectable cross-map points and returns a full frame, while render_stops requires local projections, reserves stop-marker gaps and returns a cropped scene.
